Every first Sunday of the month, we make sure hetpaleis is extra cosy.

Six well-known and lesser-known artists read aloud from their favourite children’s book. This is followed by a (craft) workshop based on the story that’s just been read.

PS: coming and going is no problem, and you don’t have to sit still either.
27D71E428A3DBB1BCE0B48A85BE19A5F:
Between the foot and the step. Between breath and speech. That is where curiosity grazes fear. That is where doubts, hesitations and decisions fill the void. That is where you move for the first time. You dance, with eager longing and innocent courage.

What takes place, in the mind and in the body, right before a first time? A first step? A first word? What journey does an action make before it becomes reality? And can we map out that invisible but deeply moving journey?

In Antes de... , Compagnie Tea Tree takes a leap into the unknown. Sara Olmo and Pierre Viatour rely on each other in their partner acrobatics. Hand in hand and foot to foot, they take turns leading the dance, guiding each other and blazing a trail through uncharted territory.

A poetic, acrobatic movement performance for everyone aged 2 and above.

Every year, countless spruces and pine trees are felled, but what do those trees themselves actually think about this? Do they queue up every year, eagerly waiting to be chosen, or do they cower behind one another, only to be felled anyway?

In Oh oh oh dennenboom , we get to know the trees in the forest. There is the elder tree – once uprooted and replanted – who is now the source of all information about what goes on among humans (played by Hendrik Kegels). There is a suicidal tree, which is just dying to be chopped down, but which, with three scrawny branches, is unsuitable for Christmas (played by Frank Focketyn).

And then the felling season begins; the tragedy has started. But this year is different. This year, they’ve had enough! Time for a pine revolution. Will the trees succeed in establishing new traditions among humans?
3227C9861B807CAA93FEACA92842ABC6:
Sorry to interrupt, you can get going in just a minute, but I’ve got a quick question first: how long does the show last? It’s just that we’ve got a bus waiting for us in the parking area of the theatre to take us back to school, where parents are waiting for their children, and now I see that the show is called Eindeloos Verhaal , and it’s not that we’re not looking forward to it, but I’m just wondering exactly how endless it is? We want the children to go home with a great story, but not one that’s too long …

Hello? Can anyone hear me? Can you turn the lights back on for a moment?

Imagination. It seems to have always existed. Inexhaustible and endless. The things you can make up! Pearl-Tailed Rats, Stray Lights, Singing Chopping Shoes and Were-were-wolf-wolves. And places! The Oracle Obstacle, The Pinball Path, The Darkness of the Deep … And the Void.

The Void is there too, of course, ever more frequently and ever more vicious. Apparently, the Void sweeps like a vengeful storm over everything you can possibly imagine. Devastating everything and endless, too. Endless? On the contrary: putting an end to everything!

Inspired by the stories of Michael Ende, WOLF WOLF and hetpaleis are creating a new theatre production. Seven performers take on the dark, destructive force that devours our imagination. Risking their lives, they lose themselves in the Great Story, let themselves be swallowed up by the Theatre, and seek a way to get as close as possible to the Void.

8FFCBA6FFD62C8C701A076ED882FC1CF:
A show about goodbyes and stretching time, about loss and longing, about how things were and what remains. Two brothers engage in an intimate dialogue through dance, music and visual art. A back-and-forth between the one who leaves and the one who stays behind.

Between melancholy and anger, deathly silence and a wild din, between bitter and sweet, lightweight and pitch-black … A story with few words that invites us to pause for a moment in a world where there are scarcely any rituals left for mourning.

The title de berg comes from the Japanese legend of Mount Nara, to which people were taken by their loved ones to spend their final hours.

selection of the ambassadors

Our youngest ambassador team consists of about twenty children and young people between the ages of five and twenty. They attend premieres and festivals, sit in on rehearsals, give their unfiltered opinions on performances, engage in conversations with creators, and meet monthly to discuss their experiences at hetpaleis.

They’re also budding programmers. Together, they watch a number of performances. This season, after thorough research, De Berg emerged as “the ambassadors’ choice.”

From the ambassadors’ jury report: “There’s a lot to discover about joy and loss. The older you are, the more you can understand.” — Yuna (12 years old)

The line-up features only leading musicians playing their sets for a family audience. A concert experience with top-notch music, just turned down a notch for the occasion. Sitting still will be difficult – but luckily, at Sonic Kids you don’t have to.

Do you have teenagers at home, but would you rather not let them loose on a festival field just yet? During the school holidays, De Roma presents Sonic Teens – the same formula, but tailored to teenagers.

4 november 2026 | Lézard

Liesa Van der Aa “Like a snail on a razor’s edge.” That’s how a friend of Liesa Van der Aa described her new album, Caramel —as softness that wraps itself around sharp edges, yet never lets itself be cut. A fitting image, because with Caramel , Liesa presents her most personal work to date.

Lucky Fonz III Lucky Fonz III, one of the Netherlands’ most beloved singers and songwriters, known for hits such as “ Ik heb een meisje ,” “ Linde met een E ,” and “ Kwantumwetenschapper ,” has also made a name for himself in recent years as a unique theater artist. In 2024, his debut novel Van de goden vervuld was published. In March 2026, his new album De zachte krachten was released.
